items.title: Joe Lyde Interview, 1959-05-18
items.q: He was playing with the Eureka at that time.

ctx.x: Before that. I never can. I think I last... Two or three hours. I started, no, I started Eads Plaza and I get to La Salle just off Jackson. And then I'm just about pooped, so I usually leave by then. And that's only maybe an hour.

I stuck with him from nine till four. And then recently I played Arthur Ogle's Funeral. You know, he, um, he's an old drummer of the Eureka. He's on the Pax record and he had both his legs amputated before I even got to town. He died about a month ago and I played, uh, there was no money involved in it and she asked me to play. Uh, Percy couldn't make it. And, uh, Bokaj couldn't, Bokaj wasn't there and Jim Crow couldn't make it. He was playing with the Eureka at that time. He, somebody had to fix his TV set or…
I don't know. Sonny lives downtown, I think.
